discoveryDefect: The direct September 9 edition and transcript were complete while agent.json, generated September 10, still listed September 8 as newest. Direct dated-edition probing is required before declaring no new AIDB edition.

argumentMap.attributedThesis: AIDB argues that September's rapid model releases make a single best-model mindset less useful than choosing a combination of models and interfaces for the actual job.
reasoningChain: Capability, speed and cost differ by task, and agentic work can increase real per-task cost even when token prices do not change.
Benchmark rankings move when evaluators change which tasks matter, so a leaderboard position is not a stable answer to a reader's workflow question.
Shared work agents and personal agents may matter as much as raw model capability because the interface determines what people can delegate and supervise.
Image editing is becoming more useful when people can mark a region, sketch a layout and preserve the rest of a composition rather than rely on one long prompt.
argumentMap.editorialBoundary: This is AIDB's attributed analysis. The edition supplied no per-item source URLs, so every consequential factual claim remains unverified until its original source is recovered.

items.heading: OpenAI claims a Millennium Prize problem
items.reason: OpenAI's paper and Lean formalization are primary company material; independent mathematical verification and prize-status context are required.

items.heading: The mathematician who says he got scooped
items.reason: Competing allegations and the complete contemporaneous record must be recovered; do not turn a dispute into a finding.

items.heading: OpenAI's user-data distinction
items.reason: Recover the exact OpenAI statement and current data-control terms before explaining whether de-identified product data could influence research.

items.heading: Academic concern about AI scooping culture
items.reason: Potential criticism about incentives and power, but quoted original posts and broader evidence are required.

items.heading: Can labs see and scoop user work?
items.reason: A useful reader question, not an established incident; current plan, training and data-retention terms must be verified.

items.heading: Selling discovery tools versus keeping discoveries
items.reason: A durable power-and-incentives question, currently speculative.

items.heading: Claude Max class action
items.reason: Recover the complaint, docket and Anthropic response; allegations are not findings.

items.heading: ElevenLabs CFO and IPO exploration
items.reason: Financial and anonymous-source claims do not currently create a distinct reader decision.

items.heading: Cognition valuation and independence
items.reason: Financing and acquisition-rumour claims are not a useful standalone LAiDIES story without a clearer reader consequence.

items.heading: Gemini 3.8 Flash works harder
items.reason: Already discovered through Google's official release; benchmark and task claims require their original methods.

items.heading: Artificial Analysis re-weighted its index
items.reason: Useful example that scores depend on what a test chooses to value; exact methodology and before/after data are required.

items.heading: Cheapest at its intelligence level, with a catch
items.reason: Per-task cost and token-use claims need exact model settings and Artificial Analysis evidence.

items.heading: When speed beats marginal capability
items.reason: A useful decision framework once tested on a concrete reader task; not a universal model recommendation.

items.heading: Meta MuSpark 1.3 cost claim
items.reason: No exact Meta release or availability source was recovered.

items.heading: SemiAnalysis benchmark-maxing criticism
items.reason: Recover the original analysis and benchmark evidence before repeating the criticism.

items.heading: Meta says MuSpark is cost-effective
items.reason: An attributed vendor comparison is not independent proof and its exact source is missing.

items.heading: MuSpark and open-weight competition
items.reason: Potential theme about private deployment and competition; exact licence, hardware and security conditions are unresolved.

items.heading: Muse personal agent
items.reason: No exact Meta product source, permissions, privacy boundaries or availability route was recovered.

items.heading: Marketplace as agent distribution
items.reason: This is an adoption hypothesis, not observed reader benefit.

items.heading: Meta's consumer-agent bet
items.reason: Durable competition and power question; factual platform and rollout claims need originals.

items.heading: Personal agents may soften public hostility
items.reason: Speculation about public attitudes is not evidence and does not earn a story.

items.heading: ChatGPT Images 2.5 control features
items.reason: Already published from OpenAI release notes and independent first-hand reporting; no duplicate story.

items.heading: Images as a business differentiator
items.reason: Useful lesson about sketches, regions and iterative editing as context routes; AIDB's business-use inference remains attributed.

audienceGap.readerQuestion: Instead of asking which AI is best, how do I choose the model and working interface that fit this particular job?
audienceGap.plainLanguageRule: Begin with one familiar task, show the trade-off among quality, waiting time, cost and control, then name the evidence limits.

bigPictureThemeReview.reason: The model-stack and platform-power themes are durable, but no Big Picture version is admitted.

internalPracticeReview.reason: Compare two model-and-interface combinations on the same real workflow and acceptance criteria rather than adopting leaderboard rankings.
